newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says it crushed Ugandan troops in attack.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says it crushed Ugandan troops in attack.

text.p: A Sudanese minister was quoted on Thursday as saying that Sudan's troops crushed an attack by Ugandan forces in the south of the country, destroying tanks and causing a large number of casualties.

"The armed forces crushed attacking Ugandan troops in the Lanya area, destroying tanks, seizing arms and inflicting huge losses in lives," state radio quoted Culture and Information Minister Al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair as saying.
"The types of arms used confirms that Uganda has received foreign support."
Sudanese newspapers said that a Sudan army commander was killed during the battle in the Lanya area, about 100 km (60 miles) west of Juba, the main southern Sudanese city.
Sudan has accused Uganda of direct military involvement in attacks in southern Sudan, where the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) is fighting Khartoum's forces.
Uganda denies that it is involved.
Akbar al-Youm newspaper on Thursday quoted Sudan President Omar Hassan Al-Bashir as vowing to recapture "in the next few days" all areas held by SPLA and foreign forces.
Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati is in Sudan to discuss the dispute between Sudan and Uganda.

Iran mediated an agreement between the two African countries last September but it has had little effect on events on the Ugandan-Sudanese border, where the two sides continue to accuse each other of attacking in support of rebel groups.
The SPLA has been fighting Khartoum since 1983, demanding independence for the mainly Christian and animist south of Sudan from the Moslem and Arabised north.
On Sunday the group said its forces had captured Kaya in southern Sudan and were advancing on Juba.
